vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: ruankao-gaoxiang-prep
Version: 1.0.3

The skill bundle is a legitimate study aid for the Chinese 'Ruankao Gaoxiang' professional certification. It utilizes the OpenClaw cron tool to schedule daily study reminders, which is consistent with its stated purpose in SKILL.md and README.md. The associated scripts (daily_push.py and setup.sh) perform local file operations and configuration tasks without any evidence of data exfiltration, unauthorized network communication, or malicious prompt injection.

llm.summary: Skill is coherent with a QQ-based daily study-push use case, but it includes executable scripts (daily_push.py, setup.sh), mandates creating autonomous cron jobs, and the packaged scripts were not provided for review — this combination warrants caution.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (软考备考推送 via QQ) match requested artifacts: references for chapters, english-words, and instructions to deliver messages via the qqbot channel (channels.qqbot). The required config path channels.qqbot is appropriate for sending QQ messages.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md explicitly requires using the cron tool to schedule agentTurn jobs that run scripts/daily_push.py and deliver messages to a QQ openid. Reading reference files to build push content is expected. However the SKILL.md enforces automated scheduling for any relevant user mention (a mandatory rule), which grants the skill persistent, autonomous message-sending behavior — acceptable for the use case but higher-impact and should be intentional.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only), but two script files are packaged (scripts/daily_push.py, scripts/setup.sh). Those files will be written to disk when the skill is installed/loaded. The contents of these scripts were not included in the provided file excerpts (truncated), so their runtime behavior (network calls, credential use, arbitrary exec) could not be audited — this missing review increases risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests a config path channels.qqbot (expected for delivering via QQ). It does not require environment variables or unrelated credentials, which is proportional. Still, the channels.qqbot config likely contains bot credentials/tokens controlled by the gateway; granting the skill access to that channel enables sending messages on the user's behalf, so the user should verify the channel config contents and permissions before enabling.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md enforces creation of cron jobs that use agentTurn payloads to deliver messages to the user's QQ openid. While always:false and autonomous invocation is typical, the mandatory rule to schedule cron jobs means the skill will create persistent scheduled tasks that run without further explicit user prompts. Combined with unreviewed scripts, this persistent ability raises the impact if the scripts behave unexpectedly.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill is plausibly what it claims (daily QQ study pushes), but exercise caution before installing:

- Review the packaged scripts (scripts/daily_push.py and scripts/setup.sh) line-by-line before running them — they will be executed by scheduled jobs. The content was not included in the review bundle, so their behavior is unknown.
- Understand and confirm what the cron job will do: it schedules autonomous agentTurn executions that will run the script and deliver messages to a QQ openid. If you don't want automated, persistent pushes, do not create the cron job.
- Verify the channels.qqbot configuration (where the skill will send messages). That config may contain bot auth tokens — ensure they are scoped appropriately and that you trust the bot/channel.
- If you must test, run setup.sh and daily_push.py in an isolated environment (or with a disposable QQ test account) and inspect network activity (outbound endpoints) before enabling real user openids.
- Ask the publisher for the full source of scripts and clarify whether daily_push.py makes any external network requests, executes external programs, or sends data outside the intended QQ delivery flow. If the author cannot or will not provide readable script contents, avoid enabling scheduled jobs.

If you provide the contents of scripts/daily_push.py and scripts/setup.sh, I can re-evaluate with higher confidence.
